sections.name: WIND_PARTICIPANTS (part 1)
sections.title: Named participants for the first ranked projects
sections.what: For ranked projects one to ten, lists the owners, lenders, grid operators, regulators, suppliers and offtakers. Each entry has a role and the report section it came from. Some companies appear under more than one role. Rank 11 has no entry here.
sections.why: Roles are kept explicit so the importer does not guess ownership shares.
sections.watch_out: A wrong role label, such as owner instead of regulator, puts the company in the wrong place. Rank 11 is missing, and the code does not explain why.

sections.name: WIND_PARTICIPANTS (part 2)
sections.title: Named participants for the last ranked project
sections.what: Gives the owners of rank thirteen, Seagreen Phase 1, with their roles and report sources. It also closes the participant list.
sections.why: Continues the same list, so every ranked project has its participants in one place.
sections.watch_out: A missing comma or bracket in this section stops the whole file from loading.

sections.name: COMPANY_ALIASES
sections.title: Alternative names for the same organisation
sections.what: Maps a company name to its other spellings, legal-suffix variants, former names and abbreviations. The aim is to link a report's variant to an existing record instead of creating a duplicate. Some groups of variants are grouped by the research batch that needed them.
sections.why: The comments say these are spelling, legal-suffix and renaming variants of one organisation.
sections.watch_out: The importer looks up alternatives only from the name written in the report, so a spelling listed only in the other direction may not match.

sections.name: GROUP_DESCRIPTION_NAMES
sections.title: Phrases that describe groups, not companies
sections.what: A fixed set of exact research phrases that name several organisations or a class of them, such as regional operators or a consortium list. The importer keeps these as text only and does not create companies from them.
sections.why: The comment says a general pattern cannot catch these phrases without also catching real company names.
sections.watch_out: Matching is exact, so a small change in wording from the research output lets the phrase through and may create a fake company.

summary: Lists the companies and agencies tied to each ranked wind project, with their roles, plus alternative spellings and group phrases that the importer must not treat as single companies.
purpose: Supplies participants for wind projects and the lookup tables used to match them to existing company records.
why: The file's comment says roles are explicit and ownership shares are not inferred. The separate lists of spellings and group phrases likely exist to stop duplicate companies and false company links.
how: A table keyed by project rank gives each participant's name, role and the report section it came from. A second table maps company names to alternative spellings, legal-suffix variants and former names. A third set holds exact phrases that describe groups, so they are not turned into companies.
inputs: None at run time. Everything is typed in by hand.
outputs: Three exported lists: the participants by rank, the alias table, and the group phrase set. The company linking step reads the alias table and the group phrase set.
risks: The lists are long and maintained by hand. A wrong role or a wrong alias can link a company to the wrong project or merge two companies. Rank 11 has no participants listed.
debug: If a company is linked wrongly, check its alias entry and its role. If a group phrase is turned into a company, check the group phrase set for an exact match. If a rank shows no participants, check that its key exists.
